name: garish-theme-unreadable
why: The theme writer can return text barely lighter than bg, an accent that vanishes and a panel in another hue. normalize() used to keep it as written; now it nudges each colour until it reads (text 7:1, accents and dim 3:1 on bg) pulls the panel back next to bg, lifts the dull accent and calms the neon accent2 so it supports the accent instead of shouting over it.

name: light-theme-goes-dark
why: A pale theme (white text on light grey-blue) is darkened to the dark design system instead of rendering white on near-white.

name: clashing-accent2-snaps
why: Pure red accent2 on an olive theme sits 78 degrees from the accent, in the clash zone between analogous and split-complementary: it snaps to 60 degrees (orange-red) and its chroma drops to near the accent's.

name: preset-palette-untouched
why: The presets already follow the design rules, so normalize leaves their colours exactly as written.
